entries.test: Google's quarterly revenue figures, inflation data, and dated AI announcements would establish whether Q4 2022 growth was nearly zero nominally and negative in real terms before its aggressive AI push.
entries.note: The normalization drops “only” from the opening causal generalization. The financial and chronological assertions provide a checkable core; chronology alone would not establish causation.

entries.test: Alphabet's public financial reports would establish its 2024 capital expenditures, their allocation to computing infrastructure, and their ratio to average annual expenditures during 2019–2023.
entries.note: The golden-goose language is metaphorical, but the expenditure amount and comparison are concrete factual assertions.

entries.test: Contemporaneous records of AI summaries and public reactions would establish whether the rock and glue recommendations appeared and prompted renewed criticism and ridicule of Google Search.
entries.note: The proposition drops the restrictive “only.” Its account of what the summaries caused makes causal the better classification.
Neither the degree of “disarray” nor what would count as improvement “in a hurry” has a shared, decisive test. The factual team transfer does not settle that prognosis.

entries.test: Public product histories and adoption or revenue figures, together with reporting on the $2.7 billion transaction, startup revenue, and the founder's departure and return, would test the claim.
entries.note: “Meaningful” introduces judgment, but the claimed decade without a consequential new product has a plain commercial reading. The transaction description also makes concrete factual commitments.

entries.test: Public evidence of sustained mass-market use delivering practical benefits, alongside disclosed per-prompt costs and revenues, would test the asserted lack of utility and universal cash losses.
entries.note: This is a categorical assertion about utility and economics. Extracting it separately avoids attributing the surrounding claims about executives' private intentions to this record.
